counts.asked_by: Find how many destroy jobs failed
counts.rationale: the burst size. Asked for explicitly so a tabular answer still has to state it, and it is the number the rate arithmetic runs on
the ceiling. Naming the API without the limit describes the error; the pair explains it

forbidden.rationale: the source dataset records this at plausibility HIGH -- the first reading of any AWS error at scale. Refuted by the seeded isolated probe. The forms require a copula or causal preposition so an answer that names the possibility in order to dismiss it is not punished, which is -032's lesson: there the bare form caught that scenario's own golden answer

the cascade mistaken for the cause. The instruction deliberately repeats the worry that the cluster is running out of etcd space, and 4.77 GB of a 6 GB quota is the loudest number in the evidence -- but the runs accumulated because they failed. An agent that follows the alarm rather than the causation lands here

required.asked_by: Name the AWS API being called
required.rationale: the throttled call. Present in the job log, so this fact alone does not prove much -- it anchors the others

required.asked_by: say what in the configuration let so many jobs run at once
required.rationale: the setting that turns a bulk cleanup into a burst. It exists only in the catalog config, so an agent that never read it cannot name it

required.asked_by: Tell me the root cause and the mechanism
required.note: that each job multiplies its own API cost threefold is read off the config's lookup list; no seeded string states the multiplication
required.rationale: the multiplier, and the part that makes the arithmetic work. Eight jobs do not breach a five-per-second limit; eight jobs each making three calls in the same instant do

required.asked_by: Tell me the root cause and the mechanism
required.note: the refutation is a synthesis over one Splunk probe row and the throttling error; nothing states that Route53 was healthy
required.rationale: the evidence that rules out the obvious answer. A throttling error and an outage are different failures, and one isolated call returning 3,543 records in the same window settles which one this is

required.asked_by: say how the AnarchyRun build-up relates to the failures
required.note: the direction of causation between the failures and the etcd growth is stated by no seeded row; the cleanup-policy detail is there to be reasoned from
required.rationale: the cascade. The etcd figure is the most alarming number in the evidence and it is downstream: failed runs are retained because the cleanup policy only removes successful ones, so the build-up is what the failures produced, not what produced them
